findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the '@'-prefixed glob in the Testing collect-only command with a form that expands (e.g. a shell loop building '@<file>' arguments), and specify how deselect ids are compared against a collection run with no deselects.
evidence: Plan quote: "pytest --collect-only -m \"not integration and not external\" @.github/windows-sweep-deselect/*.args on Linux collects without error. All 917 --deselect ids match a collected node id, so none is a silent no-op."
Class: Contradicted. Bash leaves a glob word unchanged when nothing matches it; no file path begins with '@', so the pattern '@.github/.../*.args' never expands.
pytest gives no warning or error for a --deselect id that matches no collected item, so a collect-only run with deselects applied cannot by itself show the ids match.
findings.finding: The Testing command `pytest --collect-only -m "not integration and not external" @.github/windows-sweep-deselect/*.args` can't work in a POSIX shell. Bash only expands a glob when a file path matches it. No path starts with a literal '@', so the word reaches pytest unexpanded, and argparse tries to open a file literally named `.github/windows-sweep-deselect/*.args` and errors. That means the reported results ('collects without error', 'All 917 --deselect ids match a collected node id') cannot come from this command as written. Separately, a collect-only run with the deselects applied removes those ids from the output, and pytest does not warn on a --deselect id that matches nothing, so 'none is a silent no-op' needs an explicit comparison against a collection run with no deselects.
findings.location: Testing section, second bullet
scenarios: A reviewer or the follow-up author re-runs the documented command to re-verify the list and gets an argparse file-not-found error instead of a collection.
A deselect id goes stale after a test rename; the documented check cannot catch it, and the id silently stops deselecting anything.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the arguments explicitly, e.g. `pytest --collect-only -q -m "not integration and not external" $(for f in .github/windows-sweep-deselect/*.args; do printf '@%s ' "$f"; done)`. To check for no-op ids, run `pytest --collect-only -q -m "not integration and not external"` with no argfiles and confirm every `--deselect=<id>` value appears among the collected node ids.

Class: Partially-verified. The capability is observed working on the current resolved pytest; the minimum version it needs is not stated in the plan or enforced in pyproject.
findings.finding: The plan relies on pytest reading '@file' arguments natively, but the project's declared minimum is `pytest>=8,!=9.1.0,!=9.1.1`. My recollection is that argument files were added in pytest 8.2.0 (pytest-dev/pytest#11871); I could not confirm this with the available tools. The Windows job installs without the lock (`uv pip install ".[dev,reviewbot,ui]"`), so it relies on that minimum rather than uv.lock's 9.0.3. On pytest 8.0 or 8.1, each '@...args' word would be read as a test path and the run would fail with 'file or directory not found'. Today latest pytest is installed, so this is a dependency risk rather than a current failure.
findings.location: Approach ("pytest's argument parser reads @file natively"); pyproject.toml:245; .github/workflows/test.yml:275-278
scenarios: A resolver backtrack or a future exclusion pin resolves pytest 8.0/8.1 on the unlocked Windows install; every argfile becomes a missing test path and the sweep goes red for reasons unrelated to Windows regressions.
findings.suggested_fix: Change pyproject.toml to "pytest>=8.2,!=9.1.0,!=9.1.1" and note in the plan's Approach that the argfile mechanism requires pytest 8.2+.
